verses.1: But you must speak what is suitable for sound teaching.
verses.2: Elders must be temperate, dignified, self-controlled, sound in faith, love, and endurance.
verses.3: Likewise, older women must be reverent in conduct, not slanderers, not excessive in wine, and good teachers,
verses.4: so that they may encourage the younger women to love their husbands, to love their children,
verses.5: to be self-controlled, chaste, housekeepers, good, obedient to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be spoken against.
verses.6: Likewise, encourage the younger men to be self-disciplined,
verses.7: showing yourself in all respects a model of good works, in your teaching with integrity and dignity,
verses.8: with a sound and unassailable message, so that one who opposes will be ashamed and have nothing evil to say about us.
verses.9: Slaves must be subject to their own masters in all things, being well-pleasing, not argumentative,
verses.10: not pilfering, but showing complete faithfulness in every good thing, so that they may adorn the teaching of our Savior God in all respects.
verses.11: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people,
verses.12: teaching us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age,
verses.13: as we look for the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ,
verses.14: who gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for himself a people who are his own, eager to do good works.
verses.15: These things speak, exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no one look down on you.

notes:
Notes
- v. 11: “For the grace of God has appeared” — The use of *ἐπεφάνη* (appeared) with reference to grace is interpretively nuanced, but the context suggests a reference to the incarnation. The rendering reflects the theological weight of the moment.
